Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start time (UTC): 15:00
End time (UTC): 15:45
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lin (Redwood AE), Priya Khatri (Redwood CSM), Evan Morris (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Head of MLOps, GraniteWave), Sofia Mendes (Platform Eng), Wei Zhang (CTO)

Summary:
Quick quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost spikes in January, a couple of reliability incidents in the private VPC deployment, and alignment on roadmap and adoption targets for Q2. Discussed rightsizing options (batching, caching, quant profiles), Dedicated capacity feasibility, and next steps for a performance workshop.

Topics Covered:
- Usage trends and anomalous spikes (Jan)
- Cost allocation by route and model
- Reliability incidents: two timeouts and a KV cache warm-up problem on Feb 3
- Recommendations: caching, batching, model quant profiles, autoscaling policy updates
- Roadmap alignment and Dedicated capacity workshop

Action items (recorded in call): see metadata action_items above

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Jordan Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we want to keep this tight 45 minutes, quick Q1 health check for GraniteWave. Priya and Evan from our side. How's everyboady doing?
[00:07] Liam O'Connor: Good thanks, busy. Appreciate you fitting us in. We've got a couple of things — costs in January jumped and we had two 503-style timeouts in the VPC last week.
[00:15] Priya Khatri: Yeah we'll cover that. I pulled month-on-month usage and a couple of route level prints. Not sure if you saw the emailed CSV.
[00:22] Sofia Mendes: I skimmed it. Looks like the chat summarization route doubled in token usage after we rolled the new prompt template mid-December.
[00:30] Evan Morris: That aligns — the new template increased max context and we saw more prefix regen. We can show ways to trim or cache prefixes. Also some quantization suggestions for your distil variant.
[00:38] Wei Zhang: Quick question — is Dedicated capacity likely to reduce cost if we commit? We like predictable throughput.
[00:44] Jordan Lin: Short answer: yes for heavy sustained throughput it usually helps. But we should model your 95th percentile qps and effective token rate; dedicated gives better unit economics but requires a commit. We'll run numbers after you share the top routes.
[00:55] Liam O'Connor: We can share that. Also curious about the reliability incidents — two timeouts on Feb 3. Any ideas?
[01:02] Evan Morris: From our traces there was a KV cache warm-up for two machines after an autoscaler event. It showed as cold KV — the runtime fell back to a longer path. I think the policy triggered scaling aggressively and the new instances weren't warmed.
[01:14] Sofia Mendes: We did a surge test that morning and saw pods spin up a bit slower than expected. Maybe the init jobs slowed it.
[01:20] Jordan Lin: Right, there are a few mitigations: pin a warm pool size, use pre-warm on expected traffic windows, or enable sticky routing to keep hot KV on some nodes. We'll propose a concrete autoscale tweak.
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: And what about billing? There was an unexpected spike from Jan 12-17. Looks like inference tokens went up 3x on those days. We thought it was a traffic campaign but internal logs don't show matching requests.
[01:42] Priya Khatri: I noticed that: token breakdown shows high retry volume and a particular route retried due to 429s then retried by your gateway. There were a few noisy clients hitting at the tail latencies.
[01:53] Sofia Mendes: Our gateway had a bug with retry header handling — it retried on 429s aggressively. That's on us, but can you help identify the affected client IDs?
[02:01] Evan Morris: We can share per-client token maps. I'll redact PII but deliver the client IDs and timestamps. That will help you correlate with your gateway logs.
[02:09] Wei Zhang: Great. On the ops side, can you suggest batching windows? We saw some user-facing latency increase when we tried larger batches.
[02:16] Evan Morris: Batching is workload specific. For your low-latency chat routes we recommend small continuous batching (20–50ms window) and for async summarization routes larger windows like 200–500ms. Also consider priority routing: critical chat goes to low-latency pool (maybe Dedicated), background jobs to a cost pool.
[02:30] Jordan Lin: We also have Optimize recommendations — we can run a config eval that suggests batch sizes and quant profiles given your latency SLO. That was one of the items in the deck.
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: If we do Dedicated for the chat pool and hosted for less-critical workloads, would the console show a per-token cost breakdown? Our finance team needs line items.
[02:49] Priya Khatri: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost and per-route breakdowns. We'll export sample billing views and a mock bill to show the delta Dedicated vs hosted.
[02:58] Sofia Mendes: Do you have a quick rule of thumb for when Dedicated pays off?
[03:03] Jordan Lin: Generally, sustained 24/7 utilization above ~40–50% on a GPU pool and high concurrency favors Dedicated. But it depends on sequence length and KV usage. We'll run your specific numbers.
[03:12] Wei Zhang: On security — our auditor asked about KMS and audit logs for Private — are we covered?
[03:18] Priya Khatri: For Private we have KMS integrations and a full audit log stream. We can share the SOC 2 and Private deployment security pack. Note there are slight differences in on-prem vs VPC for key management.
[03:28] Liam O'Connor: Perfect, please send that. Also, we need an onboarding doc for our second team to use the APIs — they keep misusing token limits.
[03:35] Jordan Lin: We'll share a short best-practices one-pager and a sample SDK snippet that enforces token caps.
[03:40] Sofia Mendes: About roadmap alignment — are there any upcoming runtime features this quarter that help cold-starts?
[03:46] Evan Morris: We're rolling out a warm pool feature and smarter pre-warm policies in mid-Q2 that should help KV warm-up. Also improved kernel selection for quantized models which reduces startup latency.
[03:56] Liam O'Connor: Nice. Could that help with our nightly batch jobs that spike at 02:00 UTC?
[04:01] Evan Morris: Yes, you can configure scheduled pre-warm windows for that period. We'll show config examples.
[04:07] Priya Khatri: Quick note — we saw one customer who deferred a model variant deployment and used our canary rollout; that reduced regressions. Might be worth doing small canary for your new prompt template.
[04:19] Sofia Mendes: We'll adopt that.
[04:21] Jordan Lin: For next steps — we agreed: Priya to send cost breakdown and security pack; Evan to run a perf bench and share logs; Sofia to send top 10 heavy routes. Then we'll schedule a Dedicated planning workshop.
[04:32] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[04:35] Wei Zhang: One more — any quick wins we can do in 48 hours?
[04:37] Evan Morris: Disable aggressive gateway retries, set small batching windows for chat, and add a tiny warm pool. Those three should cut token waste and reduce timeouts.
[04:46] Sofia Mendes: We'll try disabling retries first and report back.
[04:49] Jordan Lin: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the doc pack and the scheduling link.
[04:54] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
